message.content: {"caption":"A side-by-side workflow diagram compares shopping navigation without memory and with Reasoning Bank, showing fewer steps with the memory-guided route.","description":"The diagram has two horizontal workflows, with stages arranged from left to right and dotted ellipses marking omitted steps. The upper workflow is headed “Baseline (No memory).” It begins with a small shopping-site homepage screenshot labeled “Start on homepage,” followed by a red-outlined search sequence. Red text over the screenshots says “Inefficient search for navigation, consuming 8 steps”; beneath it, the sequence is labeled “Cannot filter by ‘Men’, need scroll down.” The screenshots show product listings, including shoes, but their smaller details are not legible. After a dotted ellipsis is another product-list screenshot labeled “Select Price” followed by a small unclear symbol. At the right, the text “I will click ‘Proceed to Checkout’ from the cart” is accompanied by a green check mark, and a dashed box reads “29 Steps in total.” The lower workflow is headed “Reasoning Bank.” It starts with another shopping-site homepage screenshot labeled “Start on homepage.” A green-outlined screenshot showing product listings is labeled “Hover (Shoes), Hover (Men).” Beneath it, green text says “According to Memory Item 11, to correctly navigate to certain categories, I need to first filter products ....” The sequence continues through a dotted ellipsis to a product-list screenshot labeled “Select Price” followed by a small unclear symbol, then through another ellipsis to a product-detail screenshot labeled “Identified with at least 5 reviews.” At the right, the same checkout statement is accompanied by a green check mark, and a dashed box reads “10 Steps in total.” The comparison shows the memory-guided route reaching a product with at least five reviews and reducing the stated total from 29 steps to 10.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
